strategy.observation: Ramp’s platform spans cards, expenses, bill payments, procurement, vendor management, travel, banking, and accounting automation, so expense-policy guidance is directly adjacent to the workflows it sells into.
strategy.offer_link: Expense policy templates could give Ramp’s content team a ready-made educational asset for the expenses/travel/AP part of the product, especially for mid-size finance teams that need a starting point for policies.
hypotheses: Ramp’s content team is looking for more practical, product-adjacent assets.
Mid-size finance teams are an important audience for Ramp’s content strategy.
Ramp would benefit from templates that can be adapted into blogs, lead magnets, or help content.
strategy.angle: Since Ramp spans cards, expenses, travel, AP and procurement, an expense-policy template set could give your content team a practical asset tied to the workflows you sell into.
strategy.fit_reason: Expense-policy templates are a plausible content asset for Ramp because the company sells directly into expense, travel, and AP workflows. The fit is strongest if the goal is educational or lead-gen content for finance teams, though it is still somewhat generic.

draft.subject: Expense policy templates
draft.body:
Ramp’s stack spans cards, expenses, travel, AP, and procurement, so policy content sits close to the workflows your readers care about.

I help with expense policy templates for mid-size finance teams. It gives content teams a simple asset for people who need a starting point on spend rules.

If you’re building more practical content around those workflows, should I send a sample outline with a few template sections?
